Chapter 13 · Magnetic Effects of Electric Current (page 158)

13.1 Magnetic field and field lines
A compass needle is deflected when brought near a bar magnet. The region around a magnet in which its force can be detected is its magnetic field. Field lines emerge from the north pole and merge at the south pole; inside the magnet they go from south to north. No two field lines cross, and they are closer together where the field is stronger.

13.2 Magnetic field due to a current-carrying conductor
Straight wire. The field lines are concentric circles around the wire. The field is stronger nearer the wire and when the current is larger. Right-hand thumb rule: hold the wire in your right hand with the thumb pointing along the current; your fingers curl in the direction of the field lines.

Solenoid. A long coil of many turns. The field inside is nearly uniform, like a bar magnet's. A soft iron core placed inside makes an electromagnet, which is magnetic only while current flows.

Questions
1. Why don't two magnetic field lines ever cross?
2. What is the direction of the field around a vertical wire with current flowing upwards?
